current_object.title: The magnetic dipole moment of a compact conserved current and of the declared ideal thin loop
current_object.statement:
Let the compact smooth current class and the declared ideal models be those of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]], with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]].

(a) [Compact smooth currents] Let $J\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}J=0$, extended by zero to $\mathbb R^3$. The magnetic dipole moment of $J$ is the vector

$$m:=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^3}y\times J(y)\,dy\in\mathbb R^3,$$

of unit A m$^2$. The integral is computed componentwise as a Riemann integral of the continuous compactly supported functions $y\mapsto(y\times J(y))_i$ ([[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]], [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]); it is absolutely finite because $J$ is bounded with compact support.

(b) [Declared ideal thin loop] For a closed embedded $C^2$ curve $\gamma:\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R^3$ with $|\gamma'|\equiv1$ and $I\in\mathbb R$, the magnetic moment of the ideal loop current of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c1) is

$$m:=\frac I2\int_0^L\gamma(s)\times\gamma'(s)\,ds,$$

again a componentwise Riemann integral over the compact interval $[0,L]$ of continuous functions; for the circle $\gamma(s)=a(\cos(s/a),\sin(s/a),0)$ traversed in the positive orientation this is $m=I\pi a^2e_3$.

(c) [Status and scope] In both clauses $m$ is a source moment of the declared current model: it is not a rest mass, not an intrinsic spin and not an observed quantity. The definition asserts no far-field property of $m$ (that is the content of [[pthm-em-magnetic-dipole-field]] under its hypotheses), no agreement between the two clauses in a common limit, and no moment for currents outside the two classes; no higher multipole is defined here.
current_object.strategy: Two type definitions with their well-definedness checks. (a) The map $y\mapsto y\times J(y)$ is continuous on the compact support of $J$ and vanishes off it, so each component is Riemann integrable ([[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]]); boundedness and compact support make the integral absolutely finite, and the units follow from $y$ in metres and $J$ in A m$^{-2}$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). (b) $\gamma$ and $\gamma'$ are continuous on the compact circle and their cross product is periodic, so the componentwise integral over $[0,L]$ exists; for the circle $\gamma\times\gamma'=ae_3$ and $\int_0^{2\pi a}ae_3\,ds=2\pi a^2e_3$, giving $m=I\pi a^2e_3$. (c) records the status: the moment is a model quantity of an idealised source, and its far-field interpretation belongs to [[pthm-em-magnetic-dipole-field]]; no measurement, uncertainty or empirical claim is made.

current_object.title: The steady-current (magnetostatic) regime, the compact smooth current class and the declared ideal noncompact models
current_object.statement:
Let the laboratory region and its chart, the field and source objects and the units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-sources]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], and fix $\mu_0>0$, $c>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$.

(a) [Steady-current regime] A steady-current (magnetostatic) configuration on $\Omega\times I$ consists of a field pair $E,B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ and source fields $\rho:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$, $J:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ that are independent of $t$ and satisfy the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] with the operators of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. For such a configuration [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]] gives $\operatorname{div}J=0$, and the four adopted equations are equivalent to the electrostatic pair and the magnetostatic pair

$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J .$$

(b) [Compact smooth current class] The compact smooth current class of this framework consists of the currents $J\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}J=0$, extended by zero to $\mathbb R^3$. A magnetostatic field of such a current is a field $B$ of class $C^1$ on $\mathbb R^3$ satisfying $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J$ on $\mathbb R^3$ with the extended $J$. This is the hypothesis class of the vector-potential, Biot-Savart and dipole theorems of this page; this definition asserts neither existence nor uniqueness of $B$ in the class.

(c) [Declared ideal noncompact models] The framework declares three ideal current models outside the compact class, together with the data selecting their fields. (c1) [Closed thin loop] For a closed embedded $C^2$ curve $\gamma:\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R^3$ with $|\gamma'|\equiv1$ ($L>0$) and $I\in\mathbb R$, the ideal loop current is the distribution $$\langle J_\gamma,\psi\rangle:=I\int_0^L\gamma'(s)\cdot\psi(\gamma(s))\,ds,\qquad \psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3),$$ with $\rho_\gamma:=0$. (c2) [Infinite straight wire] For $\gamma(s)=(0,0,s)$, $s\in\mathbb R$, and $I\in\mathbb R$, the ideal wire current is $\langle J_{\rm w},\psi\rangle:=I\int_{\mathbb R}\psi_3(0,0,s)\,ds$, with $\rho_{\rm w}:=0$. (c3) [Infinite cylindrical sheet] For $a>0$, $S=\{\rho=a\}$, $\rho=\sqrt{x_1^2+x_2^2}$, and $K\in\mathbb R$, the ideal solenoid sheet current is $\langle J_S,\psi\rangle:=K\int_S e_\varphi\cdot\psi\,dS$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], read on compact cylinder segments), with $\rho_S:=0$. All three pairings are finite because $\psi$ has compact support. (c4) [Admissibility] A field $B$ is admitted for one of these declared models when: $B$ is locally integrable on $\mathbb R^3$ (hence a distribution by [[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]) and $C^1$ off the support of the current; $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=0$ hold pointwise off that support; the distributional identities $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J$ hold against every test field $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ in the sense of [[def-distributional-derivative]]; $B$ has the model's declared symmetry (invariance under translations along and rotations about the axis in (c2) and (c3); no symmetry is required in (c1)); and $B$ obeys the decay requirement: $|B(x)|\to0$ as $|x|\to\infty$ in (c1), and in (c2), (c3) the supremum of $|B|$ over every compact set of cross-sectional parameters tends to $0$ as the transverse radius $\rho\to\infty$. The companion examples exhibit and verify the fields of the two axisymmetric models in this class; the definition itself asserts no existence, uniqueness, finite energy or limiting relation for the declared models, and no compact-class theorem of this page applies to them.

(d) [Scope] This is a model restriction: the steady-current regime for compact smooth currents, and three explicitly declared ideal noncompact or singular models. It excludes point charges, weaker-regularity volume sources, moving sheets, normal sheet currents and any claim of empirical exactness; the distributional magnetostatic equations of the declared models are themselves part of the declared model, in the explicitly adopted manner of the framework's singular-source postulate [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], and no product of distributions is formed.
current_object.strategy: **Scope.** A formulation definition with three verifications. (a) is algebra inside the smooth branch: setting $\partial_tE=\partial_tB=\partial_t\rho=\partial_tJ=0$ in the four equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] leaves the displayed pairs, and [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]] applied to a steady configuration gives $\operatorname{div}J=0$; no new analysis is claimed. (b) records the exact hypothesis class used by [[pthm-em-magnetostatic-vector-potential]], [[pthm-em-biot-savart]] and [[pthm-em-magnetic-dipole-field]]. (c1)-(c3) define the pairings: for compactly supported $\psi$ the integrals range over the compact sets $\gamma^{-1}(\operatorname{supp}\psi)$, the compact intersection of the axis with the $x_3$-projection of $\operatorname{supp}\psi$, or the compact set $S\cap\operatorname{supp}\psi$, so each functional is a finite integral of a continuous function and defines a distribution ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]], [[def-distributional-derivative]], [[thm-multidimensional-integral-properties]]). (c4) states what the companion examples verify: the wire and sheet pairings are computed in [[ex-em-infinite-wire-and-solenoid]] using [[lem-em-ideal-line-current-field]] and [[lem-em-ideal-cylindrical-sheet-field]], and the loop field away from the wire is supplied by the thin-current limit of [[lem-em-thin-current-limit]]. The distributional magnetostatic equations of the declared models are adopted here in the same explicitly declared manner as the framework's singular-source postulate [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]]; no product of distributions is formed, since every pairing is between a distribution and a smooth compact test. (d) records the exclusions. The declared symmetry and decay data are part of the model, not derived: the transverse decay excludes an added homogeneous field in (c2) and (c3), and the source term in the distributional equation fixes the remaining normalisation of the models.

current_object.title: Axis field of the declared ideal circular thin loop
current_object.statement:
Let $a>0$, $I\in\mathbb R$, let $\gamma(s)=a(\cos(s/a),\sin(s/a),0)$, $s\in[0,2\pi a]$, be the circle of radius $a$ in the plane $x_3=0$ parametrized by arc length, let the declared ideal thin-loop current of amplitude $I$ run along $\gamma$ in the sense of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c1), with moment $m=I\pi a^2e_3$ ([[def-em-magnetic-moment]](b)), and let $\mu_0$, $c$, $\varepsilon_0$ be the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. Then for every point $x=ze_3$ on the axis ($z\in\mathbb R$, $\operatorname{dist}(x,\gamma)=\sqrt{a^2+z^2}>0$) the field of the ideal loop is the absolutely convergent line integral

$$B(ze_3)=\frac{\mu_0I}{4\pi}\int_0^{2\pi a}\frac{\gamma'(s)\times\left(ze_3-\gamma(s)\right)}{|ze_3-\gamma(s)|^3}\,ds=\frac{\mu_0Ia^2}{2(a^2+z^2)^{3/2}}\,e_3,$$

i.e. the Biot-Savart field of [[pthm-em-biot-savart]] and the declared thin-current limit of [[lem-em-thin-current-limit]] agree on the axis, with the sign fixed by the positive (counterclockwise) orientation of $\gamma$ and by the sign of $I$; in particular $B(0)=\frac{\mu_0I}{2a}e_3$. This is a property of the declared idealisation; it is not the field of any physical finite-radius coil, nothing is claimed at points off the axis or on the wire, and no measurement is involved.
current_object.strategy: **Verification.** The circle is a closed embedded $C^2$ curve parametrized by arc length, and every axis point lies at distance $\sqrt{a^2+z^2}\ge a>0$ from it, so the field of the declared ideal loop is the Biot-Savart line integral on the axis: the mollified fields of [[lem-em-thin-current-limit]] converge uniformly on a compact neighbourhood of the axis point to that integral, and [[pthm-em-biot-savart]] identifies the same integral as the field of the compact smooth currents and their declared thin limit. For the evaluation, write $t=s/a$; then $\gamma'(s)=(-\sin t,\cos t,0)$, $ze_3-\gamma(s)=(-a\cos t,-a\sin t,z)$ and $|ze_3-\gamma(s)|=(a^2+z^2)^{1/2}$ is constant, so $$\gamma'(s)\times(ze_3-\gamma(s))=(z\cos t,\ z\sin t,\ a),$$ and $ds=a\,dt$; hence $$\int_0^{2\pi a}\frac{\gamma'(s)\times(ze_3-\gamma(s))}{|ze_3-\gamma(s)|^3}\,ds=\frac{a}{(a^2+z^2)^{3/2}}\int_0^{2\pi}(z\cos t,z\sin t,a)\,dt=\frac{2\pi a^2}{(a^2+z^2)^{3/2}}\,e_3,$$ the first two components vanishing by periodicity of $\cos$ and $\sin$ over a full period. Multiplying by $\mu_0I/(4\pi)$ gives the displayed field. Each component is the Riemann integral of a continuous function on the compact interval $[0,2\pi a]$ ([[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]], [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]), and the moment $m=I\pi a^2e_3$ is the computation $\gamma\times\gamma'=ae_3$ of [[def-em-magnetic-moment]](b). The example is a conditional ideal-model computation: no apparatus, sampling model, uncertainty or empirical inference is involved.

current_object.title: Declared ideal infinite wire and cylindrical current sheet: explicit fields and their distributional equations
current_object.statement:
(a) [Ideal infinite straight wire] Let $\gamma(s)=(0,0,s)$, $s\in\mathbb R$, let $J_{\rm w}$ be the declared ideal line current of amplitude $I$ along $\gamma$ ([[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c2)), and define, on $\mathbb R^3\setminus\gamma$,

$$B(x):=\frac{\mu_0I}{2\pi\rho}\,e_\varphi,\qquad \rho=\sqrt{x_1^2+x_2^2},\qquad e_\varphi=\rho^{-1}(-x_2,x_1,0).$$

Then $B$ is locally integrable on $\mathbb R^3$ and of class $C^\infty$ off $\gamma$; $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=0$ pointwise off $\gamma$; $B$ is invariant under translations along $\gamma$ and rotations about it, and its transverse far-zone supremum tends to $0$ as $\rho\to\infty$; the circulation of $B$ around every circle of radius $r>0$ centred on $\gamma$, at any height, is $\mu_0I$ ([[def-scalar-and-vector-line-integrals-along-piecewise-c1-paths]]); and $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J_{\rm w}$ hold in the distributional sense of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c4). Hence $B$ is an admitted field of the declared wire model; the transverse decay excludes an added homogeneous longitudinal field, and no further selection, uniqueness or energy claim is made.

(b) [Ideal infinite cylindrical sheet] Let $a>0$, $S=\{\rho=a\}$, $K\in\mathbb R$, let $J_S$ be the declared ideal sheet current of amplitude $K$ along $S$ ([[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c3)), and define $B:=\mu_0Ke_3$ for $\rho<a$ and $B:=0$ for $\rho>a$. Then $B$ is locally integrable on $\mathbb R^3$ and of class $C^\infty$ off $S$; $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=0$ pointwise off $S$; $B$ has the declared symmetry (translations along and rotations about the axis) and its transverse far-zone supremum is $0$; the one-sided jump across $S$, with $n=e_\rho$ from the interior to the exterior and $[B]=B_+-B_-$, is $n\times[B]=\mu_0Ke_\varphi$ and $n\cdot[B]=0$, the stationary tangential-sheet interface condition of [[pthm-em-fixed-vacuum-jumps]] for the current density $Ke_\varphi$ (computed directly as $e_\rho\times(0-\mu_0Ke_3)=\mu_0Ke_\varphi$); and $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J_S$ hold in the distributional sense of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c4). Hence $B$ is an admitted field of the declared solenoid model.

(c) [Scope] Both models are declared noncompact idealisations: they are not finite-energy localized-current theorems; nothing is asserted about self-energy, inductance, self-force, the fields on the sources, or the approximation of any physical apparatus; and the fields are selected within the declared symmetry and decay class, not shown to be the only solutions of the magnetostatic equations off the sources without that class. The external force between two such wires is treated in [[ex-em-wire-force-coupling]] under the adopted thin-wire coupling.
current_object.strategy: **Verification.** (a) $|B|=\mu_0|I|/(2\pi\rho)$ is locally integrable by the same Fubini-and-polar estimate as [[lem-em-ideal-line-current-field]](a); the pointwise divergence and curl vanish by direct differentiation in cylindrical coordinates (the field has only a $\varphi$-component depending on $\rho$ alone, so $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=0$ off the axis, [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]); the circulation is $\oint_{\rho=r}B\cdot d\mathbf r=\frac{\mu_0I}{2\pi r}\,(2\pi r)=\mu_0I$; symmetry and transverse decay are immediate from the explicit formula; and the distributional identities are [[lem-em-ideal-line-current-field]] multiplied by $\mu_0I/(2\pi)$ (its field is exactly $\rho^{-1}e_\varphi$ and its curl pairing is $2\pi$ times the line measure), so all requirements of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c4) hold. (b) $B$ is locally constant off $S$, so the pointwise identities are immediate; the jump is computed at once: with the interior value $\mu_0Ke_3$ and the exterior value $0$, $[B]=-\mu_0Ke_3$ and $n\times[B]=e_\rho\times(-\mu_0Ke_3)=\mu_0Ke_\varphi$, while $n\cdot[B]=0$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]); this is the interface condition that [[pthm-em-fixed-vacuum-jumps]] derives for a stationary tangential sheet current. The distributional identities are [[lem-em-ideal-cylindrical-sheet-field]] multiplied by $\mu_0K$; symmetry and transverse decay are immediate. (c) records the exclusions, including that these declared models involve no measurement, apparatus or uncertainty.

current_object.title: Force per unit length between two declared ideal parallel wires
current_object.statement:
Let $d>0$ and $I_1,I_2\in\mathbb R$; let wire 1 be the declared ideal line current of amplitude $I_1$ along the third coordinate axis and wire 2 the translate of that ideal line current by $d\,e_1$, of amplitude $I_2$ ([[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c2)), and adopt for the force on wire 2 the thin-wire coupling (W) of [[pthm-em-magnetic-loop-force-torque]], restricted to the external field of wire 1. Then the force per unit length on wire 2 is

$$\mathbf f=\frac{\mu_0I_1I_2}{2\pi d}\,e_3\times e_2=-\frac{\mu_0I_1I_2}{2\pi d}\,e_1,$$

i.e. attraction towards wire 1 (direction $-e_1$) for currents in the same direction ($I_1I_2>0$), repulsion for opposite directions, and magnitude $\mu_0|I_1I_2|/(2\pi d)$ per unit length. The comparison uses only the external field of wire 1 at the position of wire 2; the self-fields and the mechanical support forces of the two infinite wires are excluded, no claim is made about the total force on either infinite wire, and no measurement is involved.
current_object.strategy: **Verification.** Wire 1 has the admitted field $B_1=\mu_0I_1/(2\pi\rho)\,e_\varphi$ of [[ex-em-infinite-wire-and-solenoid]](a), which at the points $(d,0,x_3)$ of wire 2 takes the constant value $B_1=\frac{\mu_0I_1}{2\pi d}\,e_2$ (there $e_\varphi=e_2$). By the coupling (W) of [[pthm-em-magnetic-loop-force-torque]](a) applied to the compact straight segments $\{(d,0,x_3):|x_3|\le S\}$ of wire 2 (with arc-length parameter $x_3$ and $|\gamma'|=1$), the force on the segment is $$I_2\int_{-S}^{S}e_3\times B_1\,dx_3=2S\,\frac{\mu_0I_1I_2}{2\pi d}\,(e_3\times e_2),$$ the Riemann integral of a constant continuous integrand over a compact interval ([[thm-multidimensional-integral-properties]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). Dividing by the length $2S$ gives the force per unit length of the displayed form, independent of $S$; the sign of $I_1I_2$ gives attraction or repulsion as stated. Only the external field of wire 1 is used, and the self-field of wire 2 and the support forces of both infinite wires are excluded; the computation is a local external-force comparison, not a solution of the two-wire dynamics, and involves no measurement.

current_object.title: Magnetic dipole expansion with an explicit uniform remainder
current_object.statement: Let $J\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}J=0$ and $\operatorname{supp}J\subset B_a(0)$, $a>0$, and put $m=\tfrac12\int_{\mathbb R^3}y\times J(y)\,dy$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). Then for $r=|x|\ge2a$ the vector potential and magnetic field $$A(x)=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{J(y)}{|x-y|}\,dy,\qquad B=\operatorname{curl}A,$$ satisfy, uniformly in $n=x/r$, $$A=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{m\times x}{r^3}+O\!\Bigl(\frac{\mu_0a^2\|J\|_1}{r^3}\Bigr),\qquad B=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{3n(m\cdot n)-m}{r^3}+O\!\Bigl(\frac{\mu_0a^2\|J\|_1}{r^4}\Bigr).$$ The constants in the $O$ terms are absolute (the second follows by differentiating the first, not by differentiating an unspecified remainder), and $\|J\|_1=\int|J|$.
current_object.strategy: Integrating $\operatorname{div}(y_iJ)=J_i$ over $\mathbb R^3$ and using the vanishing of the integral of a divergence of a compactly supported $C^1$ field ([[lem-integral-of-a-divergence-of-an-l-one-c-one-field-vanishes]]) gives $\int J_i=0$; integrating $\operatorname{div}(y_iy_jJ)=y_jJ_i+y_iJ_j$ gives antisymmetry of $M_{ij}=\int y_jJ_i$, and with the definition of $m$ one has $M_{ij}=-\varepsilon_{ijk}m_k$ and hence $Mx=m\times x$. Writing $|x-y|^{-1}=r^{-1}+(x\cdot y)/r^3+\text{remainder}$ with the second-order Taylor formula ([[cor-multivariable-taylor-formula-with-peano-remainder]], in its quantitative form), the integral remainder is $\int_0^1(1-s)y_jy_k\,\partial_j\partial_k|x-sy|^{-1}ds$, whose Hessian is $O(r^{-3})$ and whose spatial derivative is $O(r^{-4})$ with absolute constants because $|x-sy|\ge r/2$ on the support; the modulus-of-integral bound ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]) against $J$ gives the $A$ estimate and its differentiated estimate. Finally the curl computation $\operatorname{curl}(m\times x/r^3)=3x(m\cdot x)/r^5-m/r^3$ follows by component differentiation of the cross product ([[lem-the-divergence-and-curl-of-a-cross-product]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]), the first term being the Coulomb-dipole expression of the cited remainder lemma ([[lem-em-coulomb-dipole-remainder]]).

current_object.title: Newtonian potential of smooth compact data is smooth and solves the Poisson equation pointwise
current_object.statement: Let $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ and let $$Nf(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{f(y)}{4\pi|x-y|}\,dy .$$ Then $Nf\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$, $-\Delta Nf=f$ pointwise, and for every multi-index $\alpha$ the spatial derivative satisfies $D^\alpha Nf=N(D^\alpha f)$. In particular, for smooth compactly supported $\rho$ the field $E=-\varepsilon_0^{-1}\nabla N\rho$ is smooth. The statement is about the explicit integral transform of compactly supported smooth data and does not assume smoothness of the kernel at the pole; the distributional identity $-\Delta Nf=f$ is the one supplied by the Newtonian-potential theorem ([[thm-newtonian-potential-solves-poisson-distributionally]]), upgraded here from a distributional to a pointwise identity for smooth data.
current_object.strategy: Substitute $z=x-y$: $Nf(x)=\int\Phi(z)f(x-z)\,dz$ with $\Phi(z)=1/(4\pi|z|)\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$. On a compact set of $x$ the derivatives $D^\alpha f(x-z)$ vanish outside a common bounded $z$-set and are bounded there, so every parameter derivative has an integrable bound $C|\Phi|$ on that set; differentiation under the integral sign ([[thm-differentiation-under-the-integral-sign]], applied coordinatewise) gives $D^\alpha Nf(x)=\int\Phi(z)D^\alpha f(x-z)\,dz$ and continuity of the result, hence $C^\infty$. The distributional identity $-\Delta T_{Nf}=T_f$ is the cited Newtonian-potential theorem ([[thm-newtonian-potential-solves-poisson-distributionally]]). Since both sides are smooth functions (the right side is $f$, the left side is a smooth representative by the first part), the distributional equality is a pointwise equality by localization against compactly supported nonnegative smooth tests. The derivative identity $D^\alpha Nf=N(D^\alpha f)$ is the parameter-differentiation formula just proved, and the final smoothness claim for $E$ follows by linearity.

current_object.title: Thin closed current: divergence-free distribution and convergence of its mollified Biot-Savart fields
current_object.statement: Let $\gamma:\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R^3$ be a closed embedded $C^2$ curve parametrized by arc length and let $I\in\mathbb R$ be a constant. Define the vector-valued distribution $$j(\psi)=I\int_0^L\gamma'(s)\cdot\psi(\gamma(s))\,ds,\qquad \psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)\ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]) .$$ Then $\operatorname{div}j=0$ in the distributional sense ([[def-distributional-derivative]]). For a nonnegative smooth radial mollifier $\eta_\varepsilon$ of integral one supported in $B_\varepsilon$ the mollified fields $j_\varepsilon=j*\eta_\varepsilon$ are smooth, compactly supported and divergence-free, and their Biot-Savart fields converge, with every derivative uniformly on any compact $K$ disjoint from $\gamma$, to $$B(x)=\frac{\mu_0I}{4\pi}\int_0^L\frac{\gamma'(s)\times(x-\gamma(s))}{|x-\gamma(s)|^3}\,ds .$$ For the circle $\gamma(s)=a(\cos(s/a),\sin(s/a),0)$ and a point $z e_3$ on its axis the value is $B_z=\mu_0Ia^2/[2(a^2+z^2)^{3/2}]$. Nothing is asserted about the divergent line self-energy or about fields on the curve itself.
current_object.strategy: The divergence pairing is $-I\int_0^L\frac{d}{ds}[\psi(\gamma(s))]\,ds=0$ by the chain rule ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]) and periodicity ([[def-distributional-derivative]], [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]). Mollification commutes with derivatives by compact integration by parts against the test function, so $\operatorname{div}j_\varepsilon=0$ and $j_\varepsilon$ is smooth and compactly supported. If $d=\operatorname{dist}(K,\gamma)>0$ and $\varepsilon<d/2$, the Biot-Savart kernel and each of its finitely many $x$-derivatives are smooth on the compact difference set $(x,y)\in K\times\gamma$ and hence uniformly continuous there ([[thm-heine-cantor-metric]]); subtracting the mollified and unmollified integrals leaves $|I|L$ times that uniform modulus of continuity at $\varepsilon$ times $\mu_0/(4\pi)$, which tends to zero. For the axis computation the tangential numerator integrates to $2\pi a^2e_z$ and the denominator is $(a^2+z^2)^{3/2}$; the differentiation with respect to the observation point and the parameters is justified by differentiation under the integral sign on the compact set $K$ ([[thm-differentiation-under-the-integral-sign]]).

current_object.title: Biot-Savart representation for a compact smooth conserved current and its declared thin-loop limit
current_object.statement:
Let $J\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}J=0$ be a compact smooth current of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](b), extended by zero to $\mathbb R^3$, let $A$ be the vector potential of [[pthm-em-magnetostatic-vector-potential]] and $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ its magnetostatic field, with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. Then for every $x\in\mathbb R^3$ the absolutely convergent Biot-Savart integral represents the field,

$$B(x)=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{J(y)\times(x-y)}{|x-y|^3}\,dy .$$

Moreover the same formula holds in the declared thin-loop limit: if $\gamma:\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R^3$ is a closed embedded $C^2$ curve parametrized by arc length ($|\gamma'|\equiv1$), $I\in\mathbb R$, and $j_\varepsilon=j*\eta_\varepsilon$ are the mollified divergence-free compact currents of [[lem-em-thin-current-limit]] associated with the tangent line current of $\gamma$, then their fields (given by the displayed formula with $J:=j_\varepsilon$) converge, with every derivative uniformly on every compact $K$ disjoint from $\gamma$, to

$$B_\gamma(x)=\frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi}\int_0^L\frac{\gamma'(s)\times(x-\gamma(s))}{|x-\gamma(s)|^3}\,ds,$$

the field of the declared ideal thin loop. Nothing is asserted on the wire, about line self-energy, about the infinite-wire or sheet models, or for currents outside the compact smooth class and its declared thin-loop limit.
current_object.strategy: **Proof technique:** the differentiated-kernel identity of [[lem-em-newtonian-kernel-curl-identity]], then the thin-current limit of [[lem-em-thin-current-limit]]. 1.1 By [[pthm-em-magnetostatic-vector-potential]], $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ with $A_i=\mu_0N(J_i)$. Applying [[lem-em-newtonian-kernel-curl-identity]] to $f:=J$ and multiplying by $\mu_0$ gives, at every $x\in\mathbb R^3$, $$B(x)=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{J(y)\times(x-y)}{|x-y|^3}\,dy .$$ The integral is absolutely convergent: $|J(y)\times(x-y)|\le\|J\|_\infty|x-y|$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]) and $\int_{B_R(x)}|x-y|^{-2}\,d\lambda_3<+\infty$, the estimate supplied by [[lem-em-newtonian-kernel-curl-identity]]; this proves the first assertion at every point, including points of the support. 2.1 Thin-loop limit: [[lem-em-thin-current-limit]] states that the tangent distribution $j$ of the closed curve has $\operatorname{div}j=0$, that the mollified currents $j_\varepsilon=j*\eta_\varepsilon$ are smooth, compactly supported and divergence-free, and that their Biot-Savart fields converge with every derivative uniformly on every compact $K$ disjoint from $\gamma$ to the displayed loop integral. By step 1.1 with $J:=j_\varepsilon$ (each $j_\varepsilon$ is a compact smooth conserved current) the field of $j_\varepsilon$ is exactly its displayed Biot-Savart integral; hence the limit is the field of the declared ideal thin loop of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c1). The convergence is precisely the limiting sense in which the declared model is admitted, and it is asserted only away from $\gamma$. 2.2 Scope: the statement is confined to the compact smooth class and its declared thin-loop limit; no formula is asserted for noncompact currents (the infinite-wire model is verified separately on the companion examples page), and no near-wire, self-energy or radiation claim is made.

current_object.title: Far-field dipole expansion of a compact conserved current with a uniform explicit remainder
current_object.statement:
Let $J\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}J=0$ and $\operatorname{supp}J\subset B_a(0)$ for some $a>0$, let $A$ be the vector potential of [[pthm-em-magnetostatic-vector-potential]] and $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ its magnetostatic field, and let $m=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^3}y\times J(y)\,dy$ be the magnetic moment of [[def-em-magnetic-moment]](a). Then for $r=|x|\ge2a$, uniformly in the unit vector $n=x/r$,

$$A(x)=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{m\times x}{r^3}+O\!\left(\frac{\mu_0a^2\|J\|_1}{r^3}\right),\qquad B(x)=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{3n(m\cdot n)-m}{r^3}+O\!\left(\frac{\mu_0a^2\|J\|_1}{r^4}\right),$$

where $\|J\|_1=\int_{\mathbb R^3}|J|\,d\lambda_3$ and the constants implicit in the $O$ terms are absolute: one constant works for all $r\ge2a$ and all unit $n$. This is a controlled two-term far-field estimate: nothing is asserted for $r<2a$ or at the support, no higher multipole is defined here, and the leading dipole term is not claimed to be exact.
current_object.strategy: **Proof technique:** transport of the explicit uniform-remainder lemma to the framework's objects. 1.1 The hypotheses of [[lem-em-magnetic-dipole-remainder]] are exactly those stated here for $J$ (smooth, compactly supported, divergence-free, contained in $B_a(0)$), and the objects of that lemma, $A=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\int J(y)|x-y|^{-1}dy$ and $B=\operatorname{curl}A$, are verbatim the $A$ and $B$ of [[pthm-em-magnetostatic-vector-potential]]; the moment $m=\frac12\int y\times J(y)\,dy$ of the lemma is the moment of [[def-em-magnetic-moment]](a) ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). 2.1 Substituting these identifications into the lemma's conclusion gives the displayed estimates for the framework's $A$ and $B$, with the lemma's uniformity in $n$ and its absolute constants; no additional analysis is required. 2.2 Scope: the estimate is a remainder-controlled far-field expansion; nothing is asserted at smaller radii or at the source, and no empirical content is added. The far-field identification of $m$ as the source moment is exactly the content of this theorem under its hypotheses.

current_object.title: Force and torque on a declared ideal thin-wire loop in a prescribed external field
current_object.statement:
Let $\gamma:[0,L]\to\mathbb R^3$ be a $C^2$ curve parametrized by arc length ($|\gamma'|\equiv1$) that is either closed ($\gamma(0)=\gamma(L)$ with matching one-sided derivatives) or a wire segment with free endpoints, let $I\in\mathbb R$, let $m=\frac I2\int_0^L\gamma(s)\times\gamma'(s)\,ds$ be the loop moment of [[def-em-magnetic-moment]](b) in the closed case, and let $B$ be a prescribed external magnetic field, of class $C^0$ on a neighbourhood of the trace of $\gamma$ in part (a) and of class $C^2$ on an open set containing the closed ball $\overline{B_a(0)}$ in parts (b)-(d). Adopt the thin-wire coupling hypothesis (W): the ideal wire of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c1) with vanishing line charge is assigned the continuum Lorentz coupling of [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]](ii), so that its force and torque about the origin are computed from the current density $J_\gamma$ alone. Then:

(a) [Force and torque under (W)]

$$F:=I\int_0^L\gamma'(s)\times B(\gamma(s))\,ds,\qquad N:=I\int_0^L\gamma(s)\times\bigl(\gamma'(s)\times B(\gamma(s))\bigr)\,ds,$$

the componentwise Riemann integrals of continuous functions on the compact interval $[0,L]$ ([[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]], [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]]).

(b) [Constant field] If $\gamma$ is closed and $B$ is constant on a neighbourhood of the loop, then $F=0$ and $N=m\times B$ exactly.

(c) [Slowly varying field] Let $\gamma$ be closed with $|\gamma(s)|\le a$ for all $s$, let $B$ be $C^2$ on an open set containing $\overline{B_a(0)}$ with constants $M_1,M_2$ such that $|B(x)-B(y)|\le M_1|x-y|$ and $|B(x)-B(0)-DB(0)x|\le\frac12M_2|x|^2$ for $|x|,|y|\le a$, and suppose $\operatorname{div}B=0$ on $B_a(0)$ (as holds for the external part of any smooth-branch vacuum field by [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]). Then

$$F=\nabla(m\cdot B)(0)+R_F,\qquad N=m\times B(0)+R_N,$$

with $|R_F|\le\frac12|I|\,L\,a^2M_2$ and $|R_N|\le|I|\,L\,a^2M_1$, where $\nabla(m\cdot B)(0)$ is the gradient at $0$ of $x\mapsto m\cdot B(x)$ for the fixed vector $m$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

(d) [Sufficient condition] If the external field is the magnetostatic field of a compact smooth steady current $J_{\rm ext}\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}J_{\rm ext}=0$ ([[pthm-em-magnetostatic-vector-potential]], [[pthm-em-biot-savart]]), then it is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3$, satisfies $\operatorname{div}B=0$, and meets the hypotheses of (c) on every ball $\overline{B_a(0)}$ with finite constants $M_1,M_2$.

(e) [Scope] Only the external field acts on the loop: the loop's own field, self-force, radiation reaction, mechanical support and material response are outside the statement, and no claim is made about the loop's dynamics, deformation or failure. The coupling (W) is an explicit idealisation of a neutral thin wire at rest in the laboratory frame; it is adopted, not derived, and the theorem is conditional on it. No measurement or uncertainty is involved.
current_object.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct evaluation of the pairings under the coupling, the antisymmetric first-moment identities for a closed curve, one Taylor expansion with an explicit remainder, and the compact-current sufficient condition. 1.1 (a) Under (W) the force density is the pairing of $J_\gamma$ with the external field, so $F=\langle J_\gamma,B\rangle=I\int_0^L\gamma'(s)\times B(\gamma(s))\,ds$, and taking moments gives $N=I\int_0^L\gamma(s)\times(\gamma'(s)\times B(\gamma(s)))\,ds$; both integrands are continuous on $[0,L]$ because $\gamma,\gamma'$ and $B\circ\gamma$ are ([[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). 1.2 (b) For constant $B$, $F=I(\int_0^L\gamma'\,ds)\times B=0$ because $\gamma(L)=\gamma(0)$. For the torque, $\gamma\times(\gamma'\times B)=\gamma'(\gamma\cdot B)-B(\gamma\cdot\gamma')$, so with $M_{jl}:=\int_0^L\gamma_j\gamma'_l\,ds$, $$N=I\int_0^L(\gamma\cdot B)\gamma'\,ds-I B\int_0^L\gamma\cdot\gamma'\,ds=I B_jM_{jl}e_l .$$ The second integral vanishes because $\gamma\cdot\gamma'=\frac12\frac{d}{ds}|\gamma|^2$ integrates to $0$ over a closed curve. For the first, integrating $\frac{d}{ds}(\gamma_j\gamma_l)=0$ over the closed curve gives $M_{jl}+M_{lj}=0$; for such an antisymmetric matrix the moment relation $m_p=\frac I2\varepsilon_{pab}M_{ab}$ is equivalent to $M_{jl}=\frac1I\varepsilon_{jlp}m_p$, and substituting this into $I B_jM_{jl}e_l$ and using $B_j\varepsilon_{jlp}m_p e_l=m\times B$ gives $N=m\times B$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

2.1 (c) Write $B(x)=B(0)+DB(0)x+R(x)$ with $|R(x)|\le\frac12M_2|x|^2$ for $|x|\le a$; this is the quantitative second-order Taylor hypothesis, the case $k=1$ of [[thm-multivariable-taylor-formula-with-lagrange-remainder]] applied componentwise, with the bound on the Lagrange term supplied by the stated $M_2$. Splitting the force of (a), the constant term vanishes as in (b); the linear term is $I\varepsilon_{ijk}\partial_lB_k(0)M_{lj}e_i$ and, with $M_{lj}=\frac1I\varepsilon_{ljp}m_p$, the contraction $\varepsilon_{ijk}\varepsilon_{ljp}=\delta_{kp}\delta_{il}-\delta_{kl}\delta_{ip}$ yields $$I\varepsilon_{ijk}\partial_lB_k(0)M_{lj}e_i=\bigl(\partial_i(m\cdot B)(0)-m_i\operatorname{div}B(0)\bigr)e_i=\nabla(m\cdot B)(0),$$ using $\operatorname{div}B(0)=0$; the remainder obeys $|I\int_0^L\gamma'\times R\,ds|\le|I|L\sup_{|x|\le a}|R(x)|\le\frac12|I|La^2M_2$ ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[thm-multidimensional-integral-properties]]). For the torque, step 1.2 gives $N=m\times B(0)+I\int_0^L\gamma\times(\gamma'\times(B(\gamma)-B(0)))\,ds$, and the remainder is bounded by $|I|\int_0^L|\gamma||\gamma'||B(\gamma)-B(0)|\,ds\le|I|\,a\cdot1\cdot M_1a\cdot L$. This proves (c).

2.2 (d) By [[pthm-em-magnetostatic-vector-potential]] and [[pthm-em-biot-savart]] the external field of a compact smooth conserved current is $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ with $A$ of class $C^\infty$, hence $B\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}B=0$; on a bounded ball the suprema of $|DB|$ and $|D^2B|$ are finite, and the mean-value and second-order Taylor estimates provide the constants $M_1,M_2$ of (c). 2.3 (e) records that (W) is a declared idealisation: only the external field acts, and no self-field, matter model or dynamics enters.
